## Brand Strategy
- **Big idea:** "Opening up the city. Bringing us together."
- **Commitment:** "Catalyze a movement to inspire action and build a civic culture of trust."
- **Tone attributes:** Warm, Optimistic, Lively, Straight-Up, Bold.
- **Brand attributes:** Good Times for Good, Local Love / Global Distinction, Coming Together / Getting Around, Ground-Up Power / Institutional Commitment.
- **Principles:** Do less to do more; Represent our talent; Design for belonging; Build togetherness; Keep moving.
- **Messaging values:** Discovery, Equity, Openness, Connection, Courage.
- **Audience segmentation:** The Skeptic, The Indifferent, The Supporter, The Super Fan -- each with tailored messaging strategies.

## Logo
- **Primary logo:** Horizontal mark with symbol (pathway of bricks forming a "b") and wordmark in a bold, inviting typeface.
- **Secondary logo:** Stacked/square proportions for constrained spaces.
- **Alternate logos:** Supergraphic Logo (large-scale, margin-to-margin), Symbol only (space-limited uses), Monochromatic Logo (single-color).
- **Clear space:** Defined by symbol dimensions (X unit).
- **Minimum sizes:** Primary: 0.5" print / 80px web. Secondary: 0.375" print / 48px web. Supergraphic has no minimum (large-scale only).
- **Placement rules:** Primary locked to corners; Secondary placed compositionally; Supergraphic used margin-to-margin.
- **GRG endorsement:** Parent brand (Great Rivers Greenway) lock-up system with and without text.

## Typography
- **Primary typeface:** Brickline Passata Regular -- custom all-caps typeface; approachable, bold expression. Leading: 95-105% of point size.
- **Secondary typeface:** Baton Turbo Regular and Bold -- functional text for subheaders and body copy.
- **Alternate fonts:** Arial Bold / Arial Regular (system fallbacks).
- **Typesetting:** Clear hierarchy between Passata (headlines/messaging) and Baton Turbo (subheaders/body). Baton Turbo Bold with +20 tracking for subheadlines.

## Color
- **Primary colors:**
  - Dark Green: Pantone 2427 C / HEX #224120 / RAL 6035
  - White: HEX #FFFFFF
- **Secondary colors:**
  - Green: Pantone 2287 C / HEX #39C82A / RAL 6018
  - Yellow: Pantone 1375 C / HEX #FF9E16 / RAL 1028
  - Blue: Pantone 279 C / HEX #3E8EDE / RAL 5012
  - Red: Pantone 2348 C / HEX #DF735B / RAL 3018
  - Brown: Pantone 7596 C / HEX #4D2E13 / RAL 8017
  - Off-White: Pantone Warm Gray 1 / HEX #F1EEE1 / RAL 1015
- **Accessibility:** Full color contrast ratio matrix (AAA, AA, AA Large) with specific ratio values documented.
- **Usage spectrum:** Primary palette for serious tone (business cards, RFPs); more secondary colors for playful tone (social, swag, children's programming).
- **Rules:** Dark green and brown never used together; brown never as background; no mixing of too many secondary colors.

## Graphics
- **Content Frames:** Ownable image treatment with typography/logo cut out from image corners. Rounded corners echoing symbol. Max two corners occupied per frame.
- **Connecting Brick Graphic:** Extended graphic language using logo bricks as connecting device -- metaphor for connectivity. Three modes: with symbol (pattern), with imagery (carousel), mixed use.
- **Graphic Pathways:** Three variants -- with typography (text along curved paths), with bricks (expressive patterns), with community-sourced content (crowdsourced drawings/notes).
- **Animation principles:** "Brick by brick" emergence gesture; elements appear consecutively in streaming flow. Animated logo, typographic pathways, and brick pathways each have defined motion behaviors.

## Photography
- **Diversity mandate:** Age, gender, race, ability, activity, geography, seasons, time of day.
- **Style:** Inviting, down-to-earth, people-focused. Showcases places and people connected by the greenway.
- **Render guidelines:** High resolution, include people for scale, realistic activities, diversity requirements same as photography.
- **Community-sourced imagery:** Encouraged to authentically represent community voices.

## Applications
- Construction hoardings, print brochures, business cards, community boards, PowerPoint, social media (carousel and animations), website, swag, signage, icons.
- **Spatial applications:** Brick inlay, bridge and perforation, seating, pavilion -- extending brand into physical greenway infrastructure.

## Tone of Voice
- Five-layer tone system (Warm, Optimistic, Lively, Straight-Up, Bold) each with vocabulary guides ("Come here to..." / "The Greenway is..." / sample messages).
- **Messaging journey:** Doorstep > Block > Neighborhoods > City and Region -- widening lens from personal to civic scale.
- **Do's and Don'ts:** Prefer warm/direct language ("pop-up parks") over sterile/generic ("labs"); "Let's build this together" not "We are building this for you."

## Outliers
- Extensive audience segmentation (Skeptic to Super Fan) with tailored messaging strategies is rare for civic infrastructure projects.
- Spatial/architectural applications (brick inlay, bridge perforation, seating, pavilion) extend brand into physical infrastructure design.
- Community-sourced content integrated into the graphic system itself, not just as supplementary material.
- Motion design principles defined early (2020) for a civic project.
- Color contrast ratios documented with exact numerical values for accessibility compliance.
- Parent brand (GRG) hierarchy and endorsement lock-up system adds organizational complexity.

## Quality Score
**4 / 5** -- Exceptionally well-considered for a civic/public infrastructure project. Strong integration of brand strategy, messaging toolkit, graphic system, and spatial applications. The connecting brick graphic language and content frame system are distinctive and well-documented. Minor gaps in digital-specific guidance and photography could be more developed.
